text:
Aisha R: Hey @eng-infra @eng-runtime — escalated ticket from MedData (dedicated/private) reporting repeated SSE streaming truncation after ~30-90s and weird duplicate tokens on client reconnect. They say error window lines up with some corporate proxy they have in front of their on-prem ingress. request id: md-8762

Maria D: Got their timeline and logs. Root message shows server streamed partial completion, connection reset by peer on our side (RST seen). Client reconnects and resumes but receives overlapping tokens (they see duplicates). They say it works fine against hosted Redwood API.

Sam K: Quick checks — does this smell like MTU fragmentation or an intermediary closing long-lived connections? Corporate proxies sometimes enforce idle timeouts or drop large packets. Any TCP-level traces?

customer: MedData: We captured tcpdump from our edge (their corporate proxy) and from the on-prem ingress box. From proxy side we see bursts of TLS records that look like >1500 bytes and then the proxy tears down with FIN. We also get SSE events cut mid-line.

Leo P: Can you paste the tcpdump excerpt and our runtime logs? Also what HTTP stack are they using client-side? (Node fetch, python requests, custom)

customer: MedData: Node 18 fetch streaming via EventSource polyfill (sse.js). tcpdump snippets attached. sample from proxy: 

```
14:12:08.123456 IP proxy > ingress: Flags [P.], seq 12345:14010, ack 98765, win 64240, length 1565
14:12:08.124001 IP proxy > ingress: Flags [P.], seq 14010:15675, ack 98765, length 1665
14:12:08.124500 IP proxy > ingress: Flags [R], seq 15675, ack 98765, win 0
```

customer: MedData: Our nginx fronting the onprem app logs show `upstream prematurely closed connection` around the same time.

Aisha R: That RST after fragmented TLS frames looks like MTU or proxy max packet enforcement. On Dedicated/private we sometimes see differences since customers run private ingress + corp proxies that rewrite or reassemble packets. I have two hypotheses: (1) corporate proxy rejects TLS record size > X or drops long-lived keepalives; (2) proxy performs deep packet inspection and decides to inject resets on long unbuffered streams.

Maria D: From our runtime logs (sample):

```
[2026-03-12T14:12:08.124Z] req=md-8762 conn=ingress-42 stream_write: wrote 14010 bytes
[2026-03-12T14:12:08.125Z] req=md-8762 conn=ingress-42 error=write: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-12T14:12:08.125Z] req=md-8762 trace: kvcache hit 0 batch_size 1
```

Sam K: Thanks. Two immediate repro steps to try (low friction):
1) Ask customer to run curl from behind the same proxy to our private endpoint and keep the connection open with `-N --no-buffer` and `--raw`. This will show whether the proxy is mutating chunk boundaries.
2) Ask them to temporarily lower `sendfile`/`proxy_buffer_size` on their nginx and set `proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_buffering off;` to see if buffering hides the issue.

Aisha R: Also ask them to run `mtu` checks: `tracepath` or `ping -M do -s 1472 <ingress-ip>` to see if 1500 MTU causes fragmentation. If fragmentation occurs in the middle of TLS records some proxies barf.

customer: MedData: We tried `curl -N --raw` and reproduce immediately, here's snippet: first SSE event arrives then stream stops mid-event, connection closed. We also tried lowering MTU on the client NIC to 1400 and the problem went away (events complete) — looks like a clear MTU fragmentation trigger.

Leo P: Good find. That strongly points to a middlebox that can't handle fragmented TLS records or big TLS records produced by our runtime when we send larger multiplexed frames. On Dedicated/private we sometimes use fewer, larger write()s for efficiency which can create big TLS records if the TLS stack coalesces. Hosting customers rarely hit this because cloud LB/proxies behave differently.

Maria D: Immediate mitigations we can recommend to customer: (1) lower VPC/host MTU to 1400 on the path or (2) force our edge to emit smaller TLS records by enabling TLS record size limiter on the ingress side (we can add config to the runtime to limit chunk sizes for affected tenants). Also recommend changing their proxy config (increase `proxy_max_temp_file_size` or disable buffering) but that's heavier.

Sam K: For a quick customer-side hotfix: nginx config snippet to try: 

```
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_buffer_size 8k;
proxy_busy_buffers_size 16k;
client_max_body_size 0;
```

customer: MedData: We applied `proxy_buffering off` and still saw truncation. Lowering the MTU to 1400 fixed it consistently.

Aisha R: OK. We'll patch the customer's ticket with recommended root cause (middlebox + large TLS records) and propose a runtime-side mitigation: add an opt-in record-size cap per-tenant or a per-deployment env var `REDWOOD_TLS_RECORD_LIMIT=1200` that forces the TLS writer to flush earlier. Leo — can you sketch an implementation and risk?

Leo P: Yes — low-risk. Add an internal rate/size limiter in the TLS write path such that before the TLS session writes >N bytes in a single write, we split into multiple writes with short pauses (or use OpenSSL API to force smaller records). Implementation rough plan:
- runtime: add `tls_record_size_limit` config (default unset) read from tenant config.
- instrumentation: count downstream impact on latency and throughput in canary.
- rollout: feature flag + canary on low-traffic tenants.

Maria D: Also add e2e tests that simulate an intermediary that drops on TLS records > 1200 to prevent regressions. We should include a note in docs about private deployments and corporate proxies and an ops playbook.

Sam K: From billing/auth angle — customers sometimes open tickets when streaming reconnects cause duplicate tokens and billing concerns. We should add guidance: dedupe client-side tokens by `stream_id` + `offset` or include a streaming resume token to avoid double-counting. Also mark this as not-billing-fault until we confirm on our side.

Aisha R: Good call. I'll add a temporary advisory to the ticket: don't bill duplicates; we will follow up once runtime mitigation is landed. Also asking legal/finance to confirm. @JuniperBot create task and link to ticket MD-8762 and assign to Leo for implementation, Maria for tests, Sam for client dedupe guidance.

JuniperBot: Created task INFRA-2259 -> "tls-record-splitting-for-tenant-streaming" assigned to Leo P, reviewers: Maria D, Sam K. Due 2026-03-26. :white_check_mark:

Leo P: I'll start a small PR to runtime with feature flag and a smoke canary. Expect initial perf regression for high throughput tenants — we'll gate behind tenant opt-in.

Maria D: I'll draft an ops-runbook for customers with corporate proxies: list of checks (curl raw, mtu ping, set proxy_buffering off, lower MTU), sample nginx configs, and recommended client dedupe pattern.

customer: MedData: Thanks — lowering MTU is fine for now. We'll wait for your runtime change so we don't have to touch infra. Appreciate the quick triage. :pray:

Aisha R: Closing action list:
- Leo: PR + canary (INFRA-2259)
- Maria: runbook + e2e repro harness
- Sam: dedupe guidance + billing note
- Support: update ticket and set hold on billing charges until resolution

Sam K: tagging eng-sre in case we need to monitor low-level network metrics during rollout: @eng-sre :eyes:

Leo P: Will post PR link and perf numbers in this thread when ready.

Aisha R: Great work team, this is a good example of dedicated/private differences. :thumbsup:
